inputs.text: Look, while the political elite jet off to Paris for high-level photo ops with OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann and President Luis Abinader on 25 March 2026, let’s be entirely clear about who actually bears the burden of systemic corruption and institutional failure. Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez signed this Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to supposedly design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, but this is yet another top-down technocratic exercise dictated by global financial elites rather than a genuine reckoning with structural inequality and the historic exploitation of working-class and marginalized communities. The ruling class loves to cozy up to international organizations in France to preach transparency, but true institutional reform will never come from corporate-aligned summits while ordinary workers continue to face economic insecurity and systemic disadvantage on the ground.
